intro: Machinery maintenance workers repair, troubleshoot and monitor equipment, skills at the center of many well-paid trades. The closest of the 25 careers below is electric motor and power tool repair, with a 91% match, while mobile heavy equipment mechanics are 90% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $65,510, or 8% more.
why_it_works: Keeping a plant running means preventive maintenance, quick fixes when something breaks and spotting wear before it causes a shutdown. O*NET rates equipment maintenance, repairing, troubleshooting and operations monitoring at 3.75 out of 5 for this job. Elevator, ship and rail repair use the same skills. All 25 matches need no extra education. The gaps are systems analysis and supervising.
tips: Elevator and Escalator Installers and Repairers earn $109,910, which is 81% more, through apprenticeships.
Ship Engineers earn $109,530, or 80% more, and need a maritime license.
Rail Car Repairers earn $67,530, which is 11% more, and railroads train new hires.

faq.q: What jobs can former maintenance workers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are electric motor and power tool repairers (91%), mobile heavy equipment mechanics (90%) and Rail Car Repairers (85%), based on O*NET 31.0. Hydroelectric Plant Technicians are 81% matched, with a median of $102,040 for their broader BLS group.

faq.q: Which careers for maintenance workers pay more?
faq.a: 12 of the 25 matches pay more than the $60,850 median for machinery maintenance workers. Elevator installers earn $109,910 (81% more), Ship Engineers $109,530 (80% more) and transportation equipment electricians $84,890 (40% more), according to BLS May 2025 data.

faq.q: Do maintenance workers need more education to switch?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than maintenance workers already have, including all of the top 10. A post-secondary certificate is common, held by 39% of workers in the closest match, and apprenticeships are the usual route into the higher-paid repair trades.

faq.q: What skills should maintenance workers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are systems analysis, systems evaluation, equipment selection and managing people. Repairing already rates 3.75 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so learning complex control systems is the main step toward the best-paid trades.
